chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'id, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Malik, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qatawani all told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah say:

The staff of Moses was a branch of a myrtle tree planted in Paradise; Gabriel brought it to him when he set out towards Madyan. It and the coffin of Adam are in the Lake of Tabariya, and they will neither decay nor change until al-Qa'im brings them out when he rises.

key_terms.قَضِيبُ آسٍ: A branch of a myrtle tree

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of Prophet Moses' staff and where is it located until the rise of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration highlights the physical continuity of prophetic relics, identifying Moses' staff as a myrtle branch from Paradise preserved alongside Adam's coffin in the Lake of Tabariya. Shia scholarship emphasizes these items as enduring signs that will be revealed by al-Qa'im, linking the era of occultation to the ultimate resurrection of divine authority and the restoration of primordial blessings.
